title: indigo_mount_pmc8: coordinates ALERTs bypass indigo_update_coordinates()
description: MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES ALERTs are published with indigo_update_property() instead of indigo_update_coordinates(), so the kept-ALERT state of the mount base class does not see them. Found while working on ticket 42b85be0-1f19-4607-b3c3-746e60317d17 (closed, commit a09e0f878), which introduced the kept coordinates ALERT in indigo_update_coordinates(): an ALERT published after a BUSY stays until the next BUSY. Reproduce in the driver's simulator suite before changing code.

outcome.summary: Pass, no defects. Fix: indigo_mount_pmc8.driver:981-985 (generated indigo_mount_pmc8.c:1080-1084) now publishes the abort ALERT with indigo_update_coordinates(device, NULL), so the horizontal coordinates and LST are published in the same state and the base class keep-ALERT flag sees BUSY->ALERT (indigo_mount_driver.c:1387-1398). Completeness: every remaining hand-written publication of MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES in the .driver goes through indigo_update_coordinates() (lines 660, 684, 691, 707, 713, 934, 939, 984); the only indigo_update_property-style ALERT left is the generator-owned parked guard (generated .c:950, INDIGO_UPDATE_PROPERTY_STATE), out of scope. Sync: regenerating the .driver with the worktree's build/bin/indigo_generator (built from the unchanged generator source) reproduces .c, .h and _main.c byte for byte; note the primary checkout's build/bin/indigo_generator (Nov 16) is stale and emits INDIGO_COPY_TARGETS_PROCESS_CHANGE instead of INDIGO_COPY_TARGETS_PROCESS_COORDINATES_CHANGE at .c:1245, unrelated to this branch. Version 19->20 / DRIVER_VERSION 0x03000013->0x03000014. Tests: test_mount_pmc8_simulator.c:700-728 check_abort_alert_publications() plus recording in pmc8_mount_aborts_a_running_slew (742, 758-759) and pmc8_mount_aborts_a_park (824, 836-837), using the shared mount_coordinates_test_common.h helpers; the two fresh_coordinates() waits guarantee the >=3 ALERT publications. Verified on a scratch copy: both cases PASS with the fix and both FAIL with only the generated line reverted to indigo_update_property ('publication 0 ... not preceded by the horizontal coordinates in ALERT'), so the test is not vacuous. Records: README.md:38 and TEST_SUMMARY.md:387 replace the earlier same-configuration mac arm64 simulator line per indigo_test/AGENTS.md:637, both 2026-11-20 18:45 3.0.0.20 38/38, matching the version; MIGRATION_STATUS.md row unchanged at 38/38, consistent. Formatting: single-line calls, no blank lines in bodies, braces OK; git diff --c

history.text: Writing reproducer: abort ALERT published without indigo_update_coordinates
Running reproducer on unchanged driver: pmc8_mount_aborts_a_*

Defect: mount_abort_motion_handler (indigo_mount_pmc8.driver MOUNT_ABORT_MOTION on_change, generated .c line ~1080) published the ALERT of an aborted GOTO or park with indigo_update_property() instead of indigo_update_coordinates(), so MOUNT_HORIZONTAL_COORDINATES stayed BUSY and LST was not refreshed while the equatorial coordinates went ALERT, and the kept-ALERT state of the mount base class did not see the abort's ALERT (it was only kept later because the next poll still found ALERT after the last BUSY). Reproduction: pmc8_mount_aborts_a_running_slew and pmc8_mount_aborts_a_park extended with check_abort_alert_publications() (every equatorial publication from the abort's ALERT on is ALERT, preceded by the horizontal coordinates in ALERT, at least two polls follow); on the unchanged driver (version 19) both FAILED: publication 0 'E A' not preceded by 'H A'. Fix: indigo_update_coordinates(device, NULL) for the abort ALERT; version 19 -> 20 (0x03000014), regenerated with the unchanged build/bin/indigo_generator (only the .c changed besides the .driver). After the fix both cases pass; full simulator suite 38/38 PASS; recorded run 2026-11-20 18:45 3.0.0.20 mac arm64 simulator 38/38 OK. Not changed: the parked-mount guard in the generated mount_equatorial_coordinates_handler still publishes ALERT with INDIGO_UPDATE_PROPERTY_STATE; it is generator-owned (out of scope). Observation, not fixed (scope): the abort ALERT carries the position of the last poll, not a fresh readback after the axes stopped (about 0.3 deg stale in the simulator); the next poll publishes the stopped position, still ALERT.
Copying worktree to scratch to run pmc8 abort tests with and without the fix
Running pmc8 abort cases (scratch copy) with the fix
Running pmc8 abort cases (scratch copy) with the fix reverted
